summary.description: Finds communities in the reviewed graph and writes each circle’s main members, related people, and internal ties into the story data. It orders circles by the main members’ birth years and gives each a member-based key, so narration can retain the same circles without rerunning detection.
summary.input: the reviewed graph
summary.output: ordered circles with members and ties

summary.description: Records the names that tie a meta story to its translated person stories. It uses each person’s own localized title first and queries encyclopedia language links only for map places without that record.
summary.input: the composed meta story and localized person data
summary.output: name evidence for people and places

summary.description: Selects the people who belong in the theme and writes the story’s title, introduction, subtopics, chapters, conclusion, and gaps in the registry. It draws on each person’s roles, summary, places, and event history so place-based themes rest on recorded activity as well as biography.
summary.input: the person registry and life events
summary.output: a themed story plan and selected people

summary.description: Collects every dated life event for the selected people and orders them by year. It leaves relevance and chapter placement to later steps because early chapter ranges can miss events outside their guessed bounds.
summary.input: the selected people and life events

summary.description: Judges each biographical event against the story’s theme and keeps only landmark contributions with a lasting output. It records a short reason for every decision, leaving the chapter-fitting stage to work from the events that survive.
summary.input: the unfiltered event pool

summary.description: Places each chapter in the wider events that directly shaped the people it follows. It leaves chapters with a small set of dated historical landmarks, and admits that some periods need none to avoid generic background history.
summary.input: the fitted chapters with their surviving events

summary.description: Combines the selected people’s ego networks into one social graph. It keeps direct ties and shared acquaintances that connect multiple main people, matching names across source networks and preserving each person’s account of a direct relationship.
summary.input: selected people and ego networks

summary.description: Reviews the merged network against the article evidence. It adds missed direct ties and removes vague or indirect ones before clustering, while using graph density to set how readily it proposes new links.
summary.input: the deterministically merged graph
summary.output: a reviewed network of biographical ties

summary.description: Turns each detected circle’s ties into a factual title and short account of its bonds and bridges. It keeps the circle membership with the prose, and writes nothing unless every detected circle receives an account.
summary.input: the circles to narrate
summary.output: a title and text per circle

summary.description: Groups rated events into places whose members all lie within the map's distance limit. It centers each place on the more important events, keeps the strongest places with a minimum fallback, and orders them through time for the story's route.
summary.input: located events and per-event weights
summary.output: selected map stops with their events

summary.description: Rates each located event by how strongly its place carries the story’s theme. The map branch uses these scores as clustering weights, while unrated events retain a neutral weight if a batch fails.
summary.input: the chapters and life events

summary.description: Turns geographic clusters into short, factual place narratives for the meta story. It also keeps only the places that carry the story’s arc, so weak or accidental groupings can be pruned from the map.
summary.input: the qualifying geographic clusters
summary.output: curated map stops with place narratives

summary.description: Composes the assembled material into one story, rewriting component text in a shared voice and choosing its narrative order. It can remove map stops that do not support the throughline, then leaves a finished meta story for later styling and translation.
summary.input: the narrations, source material, and person registry

summary.description: Derives the story’s dark visual identity from its framing and opening. It ties typography, color, geometric pattern, and ornamental marks to the theme, using abstract geometry to carry the period and subject across the story.
summary.input: the story’s framing and opening

summary.description: Translates the meta story while preserving its links to the localized person records. It carries settled name forms and event titles into the story, and makes one consistent choice for each metaphor across titles and prose.
summary.input: the meta story and localized person data

summary.description: Writes event-specific background only when the reviewed articles add context beyond the event itself. It drops stale reports that fail this test and refreshes each event’s citations from the articles it was given, including events left without a report.
summary.input: the reviewed events, articles, and story outline

summary.description: Draws one abstract chapter image from each chapter concept. It carries the portrait style and story colors into the chapter images, while the concept supplies the subject; it also removes images left by renamed or deleted chapters.
summary.input: chapter concepts, story colors, and style
summary.output: an illustration for each current chapter

summary.description: Develops an abstract opening image for each chapter from the verified life events. It considers all chapters together so their metaphors stay distinct, while avoiding depictions of the person, places, or historical events themselves.
summary.input: the finished life events
summary.output: an abstract visual concept per chapter

summary.description: Selects the events that carry a life and orders them into chapters. It compares moments across the whole record, so importance and chapter breaks reflect the shape of the life rather than isolated facts. Leaves a dated narrative spine and a conclusion about work that persists.
summary.input: the article and selected related articles
summary.output: a chaptered life timeline and conclusion

summary.description: Researches each proposed event against the subject’s article and event-specific related material. It expands the event into grounded prose, places, people, sources, annotations, an icon, and picture-search terms; failed calls leave the event unresolved so the story continues.
summary.input: an event skeleton and Wikipedia material

summary.description: Adds map coordinates to places in life events. It prefers the researcher's modern name so renamed historic places retain a current map location.
summary.input: historic and modern place names

summary.description: Decides the target-language form of each person name before translation begins. It writes one shared glossary for the life events, network, and registry, so exact-name links remain stable across documents. Source evidence takes priority when it identifies the same person.
summary.input: name evidence and person names

summary.description: Reviews Commons results against each report and keeps only pictures that directly depict named things. It reads filenames with captions because captions often describe the upload, and code admits only one result from each search.
summary.input: the report, its searches, and life events

summary.description: Searches Commons and Openverse for the planned image searches, then leaves one candidate record per picture. It searches event-specific names in Commons first so a matching picture keeps its event link when sources return the same URL.
summary.input: the planned and event image searches
summary.output: deduplicated image candidates linked to events

summary.description: Scores the shared image pool and retains a ranked set of viable candidates for event matching. It penalizes commemorative plaques and graves so polished modern memorial photos do not displace period images on technical quality alone.
summary.input: every image hit the queries returned
summary.output: ranked image candidates for event matching

summary.description: Selects a reference portrait and assigns only images with a direct link to life events. It leaves weak candidates unused, because a searched-for event or a shared place and date does not make an image evidence for that event.
summary.input: the ranked image candidates

summary.description: Plans image searches across the life, reserving person searches for the portrait and tying the rest to event subjects. It avoids commemorative objects, which can displace images of the person’s work and surroundings.
summary.input: the event skeletons

summary.description: Checks the chosen portrait against the person in the story by inspecting the image itself. It removes a rejected portrait, while a failed check preserves the pick so a service error cannot discard it before the life events and person registry are written.
summary.input: the portrait pick

summary.description: Gathers the target-language article and linked names that anchor later translations in published usage. It retries unresolved comma-qualified places under their leading name, while keeping the qualifier available for translation.
summary.input: reviewed names, life events, and ego network

summary.description: Builds the subject’s network from finished life events and Wikipedia material. It keeps only documented direct ties between named people, so later story work can join personal, professional, and political relationships without treating institutions as people.
summary.input: finished life events and Wikipedia material
summary.output: a documented network of personal ties

summary.description: Redraws each licensed reference portrait in the story’s shared line style and colors, then records the finished portrait for the person and their life events. It separates identity from rendering by using the source portrait for likeness and a master portrait for technique.
summary.input: the person registry and interface style
summary.output: a styled portrait and updated person record

summary.description: Reviews the life events and ego network as one biography, checking facts against the supplied source material and tracing continuity across the event sequence. Leaves proposed corrections for both artifacts; the pipeline applies only changes the critic rates with high confidence.
summary.input: the life events, network, and Wikipedia material
summary.output: reviewed life events and ego network

summary.description: Derives the story’s colors and type from the person’s work and the things depicted in its events. Rejects colors that cannot remain legible on the dark ground, then retries once with the reason.
summary.input: finished life events and depicted captions
summary.output: a color, type, and pattern system

summary.description: Translates the narrative text across the person’s events, network, registry, and reports. It applies the name glossary and target-language evidence, while the merge keeps dates, coordinates, links, and identifiers from the English record.
summary.input: the person record, reports, and name mapping

summary.description: Collects the subject article, related candidates, and Commons image metadata as shared reporting material. Caches the material under a stable subject identity so later steps and reruns reuse the same source set.
summary.input: a subject or article URL

summary.description: Ranks linked articles by their value for a life story. It keeps people, personal events, and individual works, so later research spends its context on relationships and moments that shape the subject’s biography.
summary.input: the article and outgoing link candidates
